t.1.194.1: Karṇa said: Duryodhana, your thinking is not sound, in my opinion; for the Pāṇḍavas cannot be overcome by stratagem, O joy of the Kurus.
t.1.194.3: While they remain right here near you, O king, like fledglings whose wings have not yet grown, they are not at all able to do you harm.
t.1.194.2: For even before, O hero, you tried to subdue them with subtle stratagems, and at that time you were not able to.
t.1.194.4: Their wings now fully grown, dwelling in a foreign land and strengthened in every way, the Kaunteyas cannot today be overcome by stratagems; this is my judgment, O steadfast one.
t.1.194.5: Nor can they be overcome by calamities, for they are shaped by destiny; they are wary, too, and eager for the ancestral seat of their fathers and grandfathers.
t.1.194.6: Nor can discord be sown among them, one against another; those who delight in a single wife are not divided from one another.
t.1.194.7: Nor could Kṛṣṇā be divided from them by others; she chose them when they were wretched and distressed, so how much less now that they are clean and prosperous?
t.1.194.9: The Pāñcāla king is of noble conduct, and he is not a king who loves wealth; he will surely not abandon the sons of Kuntī, not even for gifts of kingdoms.
t.1.194.8: Having many husbands for a single woman is a quality coveted by women, and Kṛṣṇā has obtained it; she is not easy to turn against them.
t.1.194.10: Likewise, his son is virtuous and devoted to the Pāṇḍavas; therefore I do not think that they can in any way be overcome by stratagems.
t.1.194.12: As long as our side is strong and as long as the Pāñcāla is weak, let an attack be made upon them; do not hesitate.
t.1.194.11: But this is what is fitting for us to do today, bull among men: so long as those sons of Pāṇḍu have not taken root, lord of the people, they must be struck down. Let valor be pleasing to you.
t.1.194.14: And so long as the Pāñcāla king, together with his mighty sons, does not set his mind on war, even so long, act boldly and swiftly.
t.1.194.13: As long as they do not yet have abundant mounts and many allies, O son of Gāndhārī, just so long must you quickly strike with valor.
t.1.194.15: Before Vārṣṇeya comes, dragging the Yādava host with him for the sake of the Pāṇḍavas' kingdom, until then, swiftly, show your valor!
t.1.194.17: By valor was the earth won by the great-souled Bharata, and by valor did Pākaśāsana conquer the three worlds.
t.1.194.16: Riches, pleasures of many kinds, and even the whole kingdom itself: there is nothing that Kṛṣṇa would not give up for the sake of the Pāṇḍavas, O lord of the earth.
t.1.194.18: And they praise valor in a kṣatriya, O lord of the people; for valor is the very own dharma of heroes, O bull among kings.
t.1.194.19: O king, with your great army of four divisions, let us crush Drupada and swiftly bring the Pāṇḍavas here.
t.1.194.20: For the Pāṇḍavas cannot be won over by conciliation, nor by gifts, nor by sowing dissension; therefore slay them by valor alone.
t.1.194.22: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard the words of Rādheya, the majestic Dhṛtarāṣṭra honored him, and then afterwards spoke these words.
t.1.194.21: Conquer them by valor and enjoy this entire earth; I see no other means here of accomplishing the task, O lord of men.
t.1.194.24: But let Bhīṣma and Droṇa and Vidura too, and you two as well, once more form a resolve that may bring about our happiness.
t.1.194.23: Such a speech as this, full of valor, is fitting in you, the greatly wise son of the sūta, who are accomplished in weapons.
t.1.194.25: Then, great king, the very illustrious Dhṛtarāṣṭra had all those counselors summoned, and at that time he took counsel with them.
